title: Eight complex register operations at both physical widths
surface: Reg(DT.complex64) and Reg(DT.complex32) with add / sub / mul / div, adds / muls against a Python complex literal, abs into a real register of the matching width, and dup of a literal; GM[DT.complex64] and GM[DT.complex32] carriers; eight separate kernel(mode="vec") entries
study_for: Sixteen named outputs, not one. Eight operations at two widths each get their own destination, their own comparison and their own bound, so an operation that was never emitted fails as itself instead of disappearing into an average over a combined result. That is the whole reason there are eight kernels rather than two.

Complex results are compared as FP32 real/imaginary planes, via `torch.view_as_real(value.to(torch.complex64))`. NumPy cannot represent Torch's `complex32`, so on some hosts the imaginary component of a half-precision complex result is not observable at all; as planes it always is, and a multiply that dropped the cross term cannot hide in the half that was never read.

The bounds differ between the widths by a factor of twenty -- 0.0003 for `complex64`, 0.006 for `complex32` -- because `complex32`'s components are FP16. Each output also carries a relative-L2 bound at the same number, which an element bound alone would not catch if a whole row drifted.

The abs kernels allocate a full 256-byte UB tile, `Tensor(DT.float, [1, 2 * C64_COLS], ...)`, and publish only the defined first half with `ub_abs[0:1, 0:C64_COLS]`. The physical store spans the whole 256 bytes; the defined lanes are the first half. Sizing the allocation to the logical output is the mistake this shape exists to prevent.

The reference expands the arithmetic itself in complex128 -- `mul` as `(ar*br - ai*bi, ar*bi + ai*br)`, `div` over `br*br + bi*bi` -- and calls no DSL complex helper and no execution codec. That is what makes the literal case's Pythagorean values, where abs is exactly 5, a check of the device rather than a comparison of the library against itself.

`zero_numerator` is in the matrix because it is where a control stops working. With `a` zeroed, multiply, divide, absolute value and scalar multiply are all legitimately zero, so replacing those outputs with zeros proves nothing there -- only corruption and shape do. The other three cases are what cover them.
do_not_copy_when: Your denominator can approach zero. The domain here is `0.125 <= |b| <= 12`, deliberately conditioned; no singular or non-finite complex division is claimed or checked.
You are comparing complex tensors as complex. Convert to real planes first, or the imaginary half of a `complex32` result may not be compared at all on your host.
You are carrying one bound across both widths. FP16 components need twenty times the room FP32 components do, and a single bound is either too loose for one width or too tight for the other.
Your operands leave the bounded domain. Inputs are finite with `|a| <= 8`; infinities and NaNs are outside this example and nothing here establishes how they propagate through these registers.
You are sizing an abs staging tile to its logical width. The store is 256 bytes wide regardless; publish a slice of a full tile rather than allocating a half one.
